story_report.summary: A federal appeals court has reopened Donald Trump’s effort to shift his hush money conviction case from New York state court to federal court, ruling that a lower court wrongly treated post-conviction removal as categorically unavailable and improperly denied him leave to make a second attempt. The Second Circuit did not decide whether removal or presidential immunity ultimately applies. It instructed the district court to seek a pause in further state-court proceedings while the removal question is considered.

sections.heading: Trump Immunity Argument and Prosecutors’ Position
sections.body: Trump’s lawyers contend that trial evidence concerning his conduct as president was shielded by presidential immunity and that a federal court should resolve the issue. Manhattan prosecutors have maintained that the case concerns falsified business records and private conduct, arguing that any federal-law challenge should instead move through New York’s appellate courts. Judge Alvin Hellerstein had similarly concluded that the payments and alleged cover-up were private, unofficial conduct outside immunity protection.

sections.heading: Removal Deadlines and Prior Denial
sections.body: Federal law generally requires a criminal defendant seeking removal to file notice within 30 days of arraignment or before trial, though late filings may be permitted for good cause. It also restricts second removal notices to grounds unavailable when the first notice was filed, subject to good-cause relief. In August 2026, Hellerstein denied Trump permission to submit a second notice, finding his grounds neither new nor legally sufficient and concluding that he had not shown good cause or diligence.

sections.heading: Federal Review and State Appeal
sections.body: Trump’s conventional appeal was argued before New York’s Appellate Division on November 5, 2026, but no decision had been issued before the Second Circuit’s November 23 order. If removal is ultimately allowed, the appeals court said the federal court should adopt the state-court judgment, allowing Trump to press federal immunity arguments against it.

event_overview.title: About Nvidia Leadership
event_overview.subject: Nvidia Leadership
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a leadership transition at NVIDIA after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive officer and a board member, effective immediately. NVIDIA’s board installed Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor; the selected timeline also includes Huang’s subsequent public willingness to return if the board chooses.

facts.label: Leadership transition date
facts.value: NVIDIA’s board accepted Jen-Hsun Huang’s resignation on November 11, 2026, effective immediately; the company publicly announced the transition on November 12, 2026.

facts.label: Interim chief executive
facts.value: Colette M. Kress, NVIDIA’s executive vice president and chief financial officer since 2013, was appointed interim CEO and continues to hold the CFO role during the interim period.

facts.label: Successor process
facts.value: NVIDIA’s board said it is conducting a search for a permanent CEO and will consider both internal and external candidates.

facts.label: Huang’s tenure
facts.value: Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and had served as its president, CEO and a director since the company’s inception before the November 2026 transition.

facts.label: Board leadership
facts.value: The board appointed Harvey C. Jones as NVIDIA’s first chair of the board as part of the transition announcement.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the resignation and the later indication that Huang could return as CEO, not a comprehensive record of NVIDIA’s operations, financial performance, board deliberations or all related reporting.

event_overview.title: About Nvidia Scandal
event_overview.subject: Nvidia Scandal
event_overview.summary: The Nvidia scandal is a November 2026 controversy combining allegations about Nvidia’s export-control compliance and possible diversion of advanced AI chips to China with corporate-governance fallout involving co-founder Jensen Huang. It has prompted public scrutiny of the U.S. Commerce Department’s enforcement of semiconductor-export rules, while the underlying allegations remain distinct from any final legal or administrative finding.

facts.label: Corporate timeline
facts.value: Nvidia announced on November 12, 2026 that Jensen Huang had resigned immediately as president, CEO and a board member, with CFO Colette Kress appointed interim CEO; a November 23 filing said Huang was reinstated immediately as president, CEO and a director.

facts.label: Government authority
facts.value: U.S. export controls at issue are administered by the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) under the Export Administration Regulations, which regulate exports, reexports and in-country transfers of covered items.

facts.label: Technology and national-security context
facts.value: BIS has controlled certain advanced-computing integrated circuits since October 2022 and says such chips can support military-intelligence, weapons-of-mass-destruction and military-modernization uses; its guidance specifically addresses diversion risks.

facts.label: Entity List mechanism
facts.value: The Entity List is a BIS trade-control mechanism: listed entities face specified licensing requirements and restrictions on license exceptions for items subject to the EAR. An Entity List action is an administrative export-control measure, not by itself a criminal conviction.

facts.label: Status of the central claims
facts.value: Public reporting described scrutiny of Singapore-based Megaspeed and allegations involving Nvidia chip exports, but reports and congressional inquiries are not equivalent to a judicial determination of wrongdoing by Nvidia, Megaspeed or individual officials.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows a limited set of November 2026 political, corporate and trade-control developments; it does not provide a complete record of the underlying investigations, export-license decisions, potential enforcement proceedings or all allegations and responses.

He stated that for each ship fired upon by Iranian forces, the US would respond by destroying a corresponding piece of Iranian infrastructure. This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.
key_facts: Trump threatened to destroy Iranian infrastructure for each ship attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
The threat follows continued Iranian attacks on shipping in the region.
Oil prices have surged amid the escalating tensions.

highlights.title: Suspected Drone Strike on Russian Ship in Benghazi Raises Security Concerns
highlights.summary: A Russian warship, the Merkury, was reportedly struck by a suspected Ukrainian drone while docked at the naval base in Benghazi, Libya. The explosion caused significant damage to the vessel and ignited a fire at the facility. Local officials indicated that the ship was in Libya for fuel and supplies on its return journey to Russia. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, which raises concerns about the implications for regional security amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict.

event_overview.summary: The Iran War is an ongoing armed conflict centered on military operations by the United States and Israel against Iran, Iranian retaliation, and a parallel struggle over security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict has also affected neighboring Gulf states, international shipping, energy markets, and diplomatic efforts to establish a ceasefire or longer-term settlement.

facts.label: Start and status
facts.value: U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran began on February 28, 2026; major combat was paused by an April 7 U.S.-Iran ceasefire, but hostilities and attacks affecting shipping resumed in July 2026.

facts.label: Central geography
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz is a principal focus of the conflict. It links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, lies within Iranian and Omani territorial waters, and is a major route for oil and liquefied-natural-gas trade.

facts.label: Main participants and spillover
facts.value: The core interstate conflict involves Iran and the United States, with Israel participating alongside the United States; attacks and threats have also affected commercial vessels and Gulf countries including Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

facts.label: Diplomatic framework
facts.value: On June 17, 2026, the United States and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding that envisaged ending military operations and Iranian arrangements for safe commercial passage through the Strait for 60 days; its interpretation and implementation became contested.

facts.label: International legal and humanitarian con
facts.value: United Nations Security Council documentation has emphasized that transit passage through the Strait should not be impeded, called for protection of civilian infrastructure and commercial shipping, and urged de-escalation and diplomacy.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers a short period of escalation and negotiation in late July 2026, especially threats, maritime-security incidents and U.S. domestic war-powers debate; it does not cover the conflict's full military, diplomatic, humanitarian or regional history.

event_overview.summary: This controversy concerns South Korea’s emergency response to fears that generative AI and concealed smart devices could be used to cheat on high-stakes national examinations. facts.label: Trigger and timing
facts.value: The government convened an emergency meeting on November 15, 2026, after allegations that the top scorer in the certified tax accountant examination had used AI in cheating; the meeting was intended to protect fairness and public trust across national examinations, including the imminent CSAT.

facts.label: Exam at the center
facts.value: The CSAT is South Korea’s annual national college entrance examination. The 2027 academic-year test was held nationwide on November 19, 2026, with score notices scheduled for December 11, 2026.

facts.label: Responsible institutions
facts.value: The Education Ministry leads the education-side response; the Korean Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation handles CSAT question-and-answer publication and objections. The post-exam government task force also includes science, justice, interior, anti-corruption, police and AI-strategy bodies.

facts.label: Measures and enforcement
facts.value: Authorities adopted enhanced screening and supervision intended to detect AI-capable or other smart devices. After the exam, the government said it would analyze recorded Wi-Fi and Bluetooth signals, refer suspicious cases for investigation, and pursue legislation that could restrict future CSAT eligibility for smart-device cheating by up to 10 years.

facts.label: Political outcome
facts.value: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin offered his resignation on November 22, 2026, taking responsibility for confusion caused by late anti-cheating rule changes; President Lee Jae Myung accepted it the same day.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War is an ongoing armed conflict centered on military operations by the United States and Israel against Iran, Iranian retaliation, and a parallel struggle over security and commercial navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict has also affected neighboring Gulf states, international shipping, energy markets, and diplomatic efforts to establish a ceasefire or longer-term settlement.

facts.label: Start and status
facts.value: U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran began on February 28, 2026; major combat was paused by an April 7 U.S.-Iran ceasefire, but hostilities and attacks affecting shipping resumed in July 2026.

facts.label: Central geography
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz is a principal focus of the conflict. It links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, lies within Iranian and Omani territorial waters, and is a major route for oil and liquefied-natural-gas trade.

facts.label: Main participants and spillover
facts.value: The core interstate conflict involves Iran and the United States, with Israel participating alongside the United States; attacks and threats have also affected commercial vessels and Gulf countries including Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

facts.label: Diplomatic framework
facts.value: On June 17, 2026, the United States and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding that envisaged ending military operations and Iranian arrangements for safe commercial passage through the Strait for 60 days; its interpretation and implementation became contested.

facts.label: International legal and humanitarian con
facts.value: United Nations Security Council documentation has emphasized that transit passage through the Strait should not be impeded, called for protection of civilian infrastructure and commercial shipping, and urged de-escalation and diplomacy.

event_overview.title: About Nvidia Leadership
event_overview.subject: Nvidia Leadership
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a leadership transition at NVIDIA after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive officer and a board member, effective immediately. NVIDIA’s board installed Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor; the selected timeline also includes Huang’s subsequent public willingness to return if the board chooses.

facts.label: Leadership transition date
facts.value: NVIDIA’s board accepted Jen-Hsun Huang’s resignation on November 11, 2026, effective immediately; the company publicly announced the transition on November 12, 2026.

facts.label: Interim chief executive
facts.value: Colette M. Kress, NVIDIA’s executive vice president and chief financial officer since 2013, was appointed interim CEO and continues to hold the CFO role during the interim period.

facts.label: Successor process
facts.value: NVIDIA’s board said it is conducting a search for a permanent CEO and will consider both internal and external candidates.

facts.label: Huang’s tenure
facts.value: Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and had served as its president, CEO and a director since the company’s inception before the November 2026 transition.

facts.label: Board leadership
facts.value: The board appointed Harvey C. Jones as NVIDIA’s first chair of the board as part of the transition announcement.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the resignation and the later indication that Huang could return as CEO, not a comprehensive record of NVIDIA’s operations, financial performance, board deliberations or all related reporting.
